label: round 8, phase D — the root background is the bar at rest
notes: Round 8 phase D, from Wil's annotated device pass of 2026-09-18. Two of his three asks reduce to ONE mechanism the round had overlooked: the root background. Phase A measured that the top bar at rest reads html's background (the root-background fallback, because nothing exists above document offset 0) — so it is already driving the bar, and naming a different colour per route is the whole fix. No strip and no opacity, which is what phase C proved fatal. Ships: html[data-top-bar=section] takes the hero's #100a06 on the five chapter routes (Wil's own stated fallback), and html[data-root-fill=map] takes #353535, the Mapbox style's own ground that map.astro already declares on data-edge-*. Neither can paint on the page: body keeps its background and covers its box, so these reach only the bar region and overscroll. allowedRoutes stays empty. NOT fixed, now measured rather than inferred: /paintings' bottom toolbar. The corridor canvas geometrically covers document offsets 295.6-940.6, which includes the 645-737 band, so the pixels exist and Safari declines to paint them — the stage is position:sticky with overflow:hidden and A2's visual-viewport clip applies to sticky boxes whether or not they are currently stuck. Un-sticking the corridor is its scroll mechanic and stays dropped. Also not possible on any page: a see-through bar at rest, since the render surface starts at document offset 0, below the bar.
